why: Coverage code-references ADDED after R-B, because a coverage claim
acquired a surface or an ambiguous historical pointer was replaced by
qualified concrete surfaces. The R6 -> R7 ledgers record RENAMES and
assert that R-B 'moved paths, it did not add, drop or merge an owner',
so an addition must not be recorded by rewriting them — the same
reasoning that records retired live pointers in
`coverage_code_ref_retirements.json` rather than in a ledger edit.
With this file the invariant is still exact and still provable from
R6's total of 313: every reference a manifest names today is either
in the R7 ledger, or retired there, or added here with the authority
that added it and the reason.

additions.reason: NECB 2025's 8.4.1.2 row claims that on the 8.4.4 archetype-EUI path the (3) and (4)(a) verdicts are applied per thermal block and composed into the determination. Its two existing pointers, `compliance.py#_evaluate` and `#_evaluate_unmet`, are preserved forwarding surfaces for the REFERENCE path and are not on the EUI path's executed call path — `_eui_compliance` calls `path.evaluate_unmet_8_4_4` directly. Stage 9's evidence rule makes a forwarding pointer not executed for the claim substantively false, so the claim needed this pointer. I first removed it instead, reasoning that the R7 ledger forbade additions; Sol ruled that the ledger is a historical migration record, not a rule that this product may never acquire a coverage pointer.

Both edition snapshots gained the previously absent 3.2.3.3 coverage row. The public extent lookup now expresses Sentence (4)'s embedded-system override rather than deciding every floor from HDD alone.

Both edition snapshots gained the previously absent 3.2.3.3 coverage row. This inventory preserves exact radiant-surface applicability before reference-HVAC teardown and recognizes internal-source floor constructions.
Both edition snapshots gained the previously absent 3.2.3.3 coverage row. This application site selects full-area insulation for detected embedded floors and emits the unresolved-topology warning.

Both edition snapshots gained the previously absent 3.2.3.3 coverage row. The performance path executes the applicability inventory before HVAC replacement and hands it to the cloned reference envelope.

Both editions' 8.4.2.2.(4) rows formerly named the ambiguous unqualified `execute`, which resolved first to Backend.execute's abstract NotImplementedError stub. Local.execute is the default concrete path that translates the model and invokes the provisioned EnergyPlus binary; EnergyPlus's ANSI/ASHRAE 140 testing remains the conformance authority stated by the row.

The same requirement applies when the supported remote backend is selected. Remote.execute is the concrete orchestration path that prepares, submits, polls and downloads that EnergyPlus run, so both concrete execution paths are named rather than presenting the default local path as the only implementation.

Both editions' 3.2.3.3 coverage rows now name the implementation that turns the submitted slab field and measured exposed perimeter into D-32's disclosed equivalent-UA reference construction. This is a new realization of the existing requirement, not an R-B rename, so it is recorded as an addition rather than rewriting either historical migration ledger.

Both editions' 3.2.3.3 coverage rows now name the phase-2b call site that measures the exposed perimeter before either model changes, gates only method-neutral input defects, applies symmetric Kiva where supported, and hands the same measurements to the reference equivalent-UA applier.
